subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class skill-creation authority/routing extension point, and if so should it be a plugin hook, tool-policy convention, or config-backed authority model?
rationale: The remaining work changes model tool selection, Plugin SDK semantics, and Skill Workshop governance, so source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the permanent product/API boundary.

options.title: Add a narrow authority extension
options.body: Create a supported hook or authority model that lets custom skill-creation workflows run before Skill Workshop proposal persistence while preserving one write boundary.

options.title: Document tool-policy composition only
options.body: Use existing `tools.deny` and custom plugin tools as the supported workaround, accepting that OpenClaw will not guarantee pre-selection routing.

options.title: Keep Skill Workshop direct
options.body: Decline first-class custom workflow authority and keep Skill Workshop as the only model-facing durable skill creation path.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow authority extension
recommendation.body: Create a supported hook or authority model that lets custom skill-creation workflows run before Skill Workshop proposal persistence while preserving one write boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their Skill Workshop proposal-store, CLI, Gateway, and write-boundary history is the strongest feature-history signal for choosing the extension boundary.
